GracePrinciples.Principle: Test-first: every behavior change starts with a failing bun test that encodes the acceptance criterion.
Blocking gates: format, lint, typecheck, tests and grace lint block commits and reviews.
Keep semantic anchors stable and grep-friendly.
Model only what exists: no module without code, no code module without a verification entry.

P01 One Fundamental Entity: Locus: A system is described by one fundamental entity, the Locus, and every other semantic concept is defined as an extension, a relation, a capability or a derived view of Loci.
P02 Extensions Are Composable: Meaning is added to Loci through semantic extensions that combine explicitly into a Locus kind, and an incompatible combination is reported rather than silently merged.
P03 No Code Outside Semantics: Every managed code file belongs to a discoverable Locus owner, and a file without an owner is a reported finding, not a silent gap.

P04 Executable Code Is the Source of Semantic Truth: The description of what a system is comes from the code and its typed definitions, and prose documentation is derived from or linked to them, never the reverse.

P05 Agents Access Knowledge Through Semantic APIs: Agents read and change a system through typed introspection and capability APIs over the semantic model, not by searching raw files or running untyped commands.

P06 Archetypes Provide Specialized Verification: Verification rules are grouped into Archetypes that apply to the Loci whose composition includes given extensions, so each kind of Locus is checked against the rules that fit it.

P07 No Universal Correctness Algorithm: Telos does not offer one correctness test for every system; correctness is defined per Archetype, and the kernel does not claim that a model is correct in general.
P08 No Mandatory Application Architecture: Telos describes and checks architecture that a project chooses; it does not require a particular layering, folder structure or application pattern.

P09 No Duplication of Existing Frameworks: Telos does not reimplement general-purpose frameworks such as a type system, a test runner, a schema library or a build tool; it uses them and adds only the semantic layer they lack.
P10 No Unnecessary Abstraction Layers: Telos adds an abstraction only when a concrete need requires it, and each layer must have a caller that needs it, so the code stays direct and readable.
P11 No Compatibility for Obsolete Mistakes: Telos does not keep compatibility layers for an earlier model that was a mistake; it replaces the mistake and records the change.

P12 No Manually Synchronized Duplicate Models: A fact about the system is recorded once, and a second description is either generated from the first or checked against it by a tool that reports drift.
P13 No Unverified Claims as Guarantees: A statement about the system is presented as a guarantee only when a rule produced it by a real check, and every other statement carries its knowledge status.
P14 No AI Dependency in the Semantic Kernel: The semantic kernel is deterministic and imports no model provider; AI agents use the kernel through its APIs and never become a part of it.
P15 No Arbitrary Agent Privileges: An agent can invoke a capability only when a relation in the model grants that invocation, and it has no ambient access to tools or data beyond those grants.
P16 No Speculative Implementation: Telos implements a concept only when a current use needs it, and future concepts are described as direction, not built as code.
